scenes.heading: Biological molecules
scenes.sub: Why shape decides what a molecule can do
scenes.say: Why is cellulose tough but starch easy to digest? Why can one amino acid change cause sickle cell disease? It all comes down to how the four big molecules of life are built.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.breaks: The water isn't a separate part: it's made from an –OH on one monomer and an –H on the other, and enzymes catalyse each step.
scenes.say: Think of a train. Each carriage is a monomer, and the whole train is the polymer. Each time you couple two carriages, one water molecule is given off. That's condensation. Uncoupling needs water added back. That's hydrolysis.

scenes.heading: Worked example
scenes.question: A polypeptide of 150 amino acids is made. How many water molecules are released?
lines: A chain of n monomers has n − 1 bonds
scenes.say: A polypeptide of one hundred and fifty amino acids is made. A chain of n monomers has n minus one bonds. So there are one hundred and forty-nine peptide bonds, and one hundred and forty-nine waters released.
scenes.caption: A polypeptide of 150 amino acids is made. A chain of n monomers has n − 1 bonds. So there are 149 peptide bonds, and 149 waters released.

scenes.heading: Same glucose, different jobs
scenes.say: Alpha glucose is for a store: starch coils into a compact helix, and glycogen branches. Beta glucose builds: in cellulose every second glucose is flipped, so chains are straight and bond together into strong fibres. We can't digest them, so cellulose is fibre.

scenes.heading: Lipids
points: Cis double bonds kink the chain: liquid oil
scenes.say: Lipids are hydrophobic. Saturated means straight means solid: no double bonds, so tails pack tightly, like butter. Kinked unsaturated fats stay liquid, like olive oil. Phospholipids form the bilayer of every membrane. And a triglyceride is not a polymer.

scenes.heading: Four levels of protein structure
scenes.say: Picture a bead necklace. Primary structure is the order of beads, held by peptide bonds. Secondary is coils and pleats, from backbone hydrogen bonds. Tertiary is the 3D fold, held by R group bonds. Quaternary is several chains together, like haemoglobin.

scenes.heading: Chargaff's rule
scenes.question: Double-stranded DNA is 22% adenine. Find the other bases.
lines: A pairs with T, so T = 22%
scenes.say: Double-stranded DNA is twenty-two percent adenine. A pairs with T, so T is also twenty-two. That's forty-four percent, leaving fifty-six for G and C: twenty-eight percent each. This only works for double-stranded DNA.
scenes.caption: Double-stranded DNA is 22% adenine. A pairs with T, so T is also 22%. That's 44%, leaving 56% for G and C: 28% each. This only works for double-stranded DNA.

points: A–T: 2 H bonds; G–C: 3 H bonds
scenes.say: Quick recap. Condensation builds polymers and hydrolysis breaks them. Alpha glucose stores, beta glucose builds. Saturated fats are straight and solid. Proteins have four levels of structure. G C pairs have three hydrogen bonds, A T pairs two. Now try the practice questions!
